subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the custom yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context stalls despite possible prompt-ordering and session-timing changes?
rationale: The patch is well-proven and has no identified correctness defect, but it changes compatibility-sensitive bootstrap context construction and hook scheduling, so automation should not choose the upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
options.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, require a current-main rebase with green exact-head checks, and merge the focused fix.

options.title: Require Live Channel Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but require a current-head embedded-run or channel-latency transcript showing channel I/O remains responsive during bootstrap.

options.title: Pause For Broader Architecture
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching over a custom walker and cooperative yielding.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
recommendation.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, require a current-main rebase with green exact-head checks, and merge the focused fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged history spans the hook registry, bootstrap hook path, and guarded workspace reader affected by this decision.
